YOUR COMMUNITY. YOUR CODE.

Meet chatbox.js

Give your community a bot with personality.
One import for messages, embeds, DMs, and moderation.

Node.js 20.3+No dependenciesES modules

Buttons, commands & forms

Apps can open a custom form from a message button or a slash command. The form identifies the receiving bot. Submissions go only to that bot; an ephemeral reply is visible only to the submitting member.

Download a complete application-form bot. Upload it in Bot Studio. Under Slash commands, enter apply | Open an application form and save. Type /apply in chat, or send !apply to get a button.

Form handler 
import { Client, Events, ModalBuilder, TextInputBuilder,
  ActionRowBuilder, TextInputStyle } from 'chatbox.js';
const client = new Client();
client.on(Events.InteractionCreate, async interaction => {
  if (interaction.isChatInputCommand() && interaction.commandName === 'apply') {
    await interaction.showModal(new ModalBuilder()
      .setCustomId('application').setTitle('Access request')
      .addComponents(new ActionRowBuilder().addComponents(
        new TextInputBuilder().setCustomId('reason')
          .setLabel('Why would you like access?')
          .setStyle(TextInputStyle.Paragraph).setMaxLength(1000)
      )));
  } else if (interaction.isModalSubmit()) {
    const reason = interaction.fields.getTextInputValue('reason');
    await interaction.reply({content: 'Thanks for your response!', ephemeral: true});
  }
});
await client.login();

For Node.js or Workers, import ./chatbox.js. Register commands once with await client.commands.set([{name:'apply',description:'Open an application form'}]) after login, or use Studio. Registration replaces that bot’s command list. Do not register again on every message.

Commands accept optional free text after the name: read it with interaction.options.getString('input'). Typed Discord command options are not implemented. Buttons use ButtonBuilder, ButtonStyle, and ActionRowBuilder; send rows in the message’s components array. Link buttons require HTTPS.

Forms support 1–5 text fields, required/optional fields, placeholders, short/paragraph styles and maximum lengths. Each interaction can be answered once within 15 minutes. The chat waits up to 90 seconds; keep handlers short. Hosted bots receive events immediately when capacity allows; Workers cron normally adds up to one minute of latency. Self-hosted polling claims interactions once, so failed handlers are not automatically replayed.

Manage your community

These methods work in hosted and self-hosted bots. Channel access, AutoMod, slowmode, timeouts and role hierarchy remain enforced by the server.

Common operations 
await client.profile.edit({display_name:'Helper',bio:'Here to help.'});
const members = await client.members.fetch();
const roles = await client.roles.fetch(); // Read only: only root assigns roles.
await client.members.setNickname(userId, 'New nickname');
const history = await client.members.standing(userId);
const created = await client.channels.create({name:'projects',is_private:true});
await client.channels.edit(created.id, {slowmode_seconds:10});
await client.channels.setPermission({channel_id:created.id,
  subject:'user:' + userId,permission:'view',value:true});
await client.channels.archive(created.id);
await client.categories.create({name:'Projects',sort_order:2});
const categories = await client.categories.fetch();
await client.categories.delete(categoryId); // Channels are preserved.
const thread = await client.threads.create({channel_id:channelId,name:'Ideas'});
await client.threads.archive({id:thread.id,archived:true});
const poll = await client.polls.create({channel_id:channelId,question:'Which day?',
  answers:[{text:'Saturday'},{text:'Sunday'}],duration_hours:24,multiple:false});
const [results] = await client.polls.fetch(channelId,[poll.id]);
await client.polls.vote({id:poll.id,choices:[results.options[0].id]});
await client.polls.close(poll.id);

Root must explicitly grant manage_channels for channels/categories and manage_members for nicknames. The bot owner must also be an Administrator or higher for channel management, or Moderator or higher for nicknames. Moderation history requires moderate. No bot can assign staff roles.

The generic endpoint POST /v1/actions accepts {action,payload} and the same Authorization: Bot … header. It uses the same permission checks as SDK methods; it does not expose arbitrary SQL or administrator credentials.

CHATBOX has no voice/video gateway, Discord servers, Discord OAuth, billing, external app installation, or Discord moderation infrastructure. Those Discord APIs cannot be provided by this app. Components currently support buttons and text-input forms; select menus, follow-up interaction webhooks, and typed slash-command options are not implemented.

Run your bot from the dashboard

Open Server settings → Apps & Bots → Open Bot Studio. Upload a JavaScript file or type in the editor. It includes highlighting, line numbers, and autocomplete. Save draft saves your work without changing the running bot. Publish & run 24/7 activates it. You can close your browser; Supabase handles new messages for you.

Hosted bot · no token needed 
import { Client, Events, EmbedBuilder } from 'chatbox.js';
const client = new Client();
client.on(Events.MessageCreate, async message => {
  if (message.content === '!ping') await message.reply('Pong!');
  if (message.content === '!dm') await message.author.send('Hello!');
});
await client.login();

Hosted bots receive new human messages in channels and DMs they can access. Bot messages do not trigger other hosted bots, preventing reply loops. Your published script starts fresh for each event. Replies, embeds, DMs, word matching, and authorized moderation use the same API as self-hosted bots.

Execution limits: each event gets 8 API calls, 8 MB of JavaScript memory, approximately 150 ms of script CPU time, and an 8-second deadline. Scripts can be up to 80,000 characters. Only chatbox.js can be imported. External fetch, npm packages, timers, persistent global variables, and startup events require the Node.js option below. A failed event is logged and is not automatically replayed, avoiding duplicate replies or moderation actions.

Logs: refresh Recent executions to see the last 20 runs. Logs are retained for 7 days. Stop hosting pauses future events; an API action already in progress may finish. Publishing a new version cancels pending events from the old version.

Hosting stays available without an open dashboard and wakes on messages instead of polling channel history. Queued work has a once-per-minute recovery check. Backlogs can take longer to process. Availability and usage still follow your Supabase project's quotas.

To switch to your own host, download your script and chatbox.js, then set your bot token as shown below. Stop dashboard hosting before starting the same bot elsewhere to avoid duplicate replies.

01

Self-host with Node.js

Create a bot in Server settings → Apps & Bots. Save its token in your environment. Run your bot with Node.js 20.3 or newer on your computer or a server.

GitHub Pages hosts the chat UI and this guide. With this option, your bot is a separate Node process. Dashboard hosting above is also available.

1. Download three files

↓ chatbox.js↓ example-bot.mjs↓ package.json

Put them in the same folder. The package file contains "type": "module". No npm dependencies are required. This is a local SDK download, not an npm package named chatbox.js.

2. Set your token and run

PowerShell 
$env:CHATBOX_BOT_TOKEN = "your-bot-token"
node example-bot.mjs

Send !ping, !embed, or !dm in a channel the bot can see.

3. Your first bot

JavaScript 
import { Client, Events, EmbedBuilder, Colors } from './chatbox.js';
const client = new Client();
client.once(Events.ClientReady, () => console.log(`Ready as ${client.user.displayName}`));
client.on(Events.Error, error => console.error(error.message));
client.on(Events.MessageCreate, async message => {
  if (message.author.bot) return;
  if (message.content === '!ping') await message.reply('Pong!');
  if (message.content === '!embed') {
    const embed = new EmbedBuilder().setColor(Colors.Blurple)
      .setTitle('Hello from CHATBOX').setDescription('One import. Your own bot.')
      .addFields({name:'Commands',value:'`!ping` · `!embed` · `!dm`'})
      .setFooter({text:'Built with chatbox.js'}).setTimestamp();
    await message.reply({embeds:[embed]});
  }
  if (message.content === '!dm') await message.author.send('You asked for a DM. Here it is!');
});
process.once('SIGINT', () => client.destroy());
await client.login();

02

Messages & events

messageCreate gives you a message with content, author, channel, channelId, embeds, id, and createdTimestamp. Ignore bot authors to avoid reply loops.

JavaScript 
client.on(Events.MessageCreate, async message => {
  if (message.author.bot) return;
  if (message.content === '!hello') {
    const sent = await message.reply('Hello!');
    await sent.edit('Hello, everyone!');
    // await sent.delete();
  }
});

// Send to a known channel ID (the ID is in the chat URL hash).
const channel = await client.channels.fetch('YOUR_CHANNEL_ID');
await channel.send('A new update is ready.');
How events work: one HTTP poll checks all channels the bot may view, normally every 3 seconds. This is not Discord’s WebSocket Gateway. New messages are delivered; edit/delete events, typing, presence, voice, reactions, slash-command registration, and interactive components are not implemented.

Use client.once(Events.ClientReady, handler), client.on(Events.Error, handler), and client.destroy() to manage the process. Channel fetch returns a Map when no ID is provided.

03

Rich embeds

Use EmbedBuilder for colored cards with a title, Markdown description, fields, author, footer, timestamp, thumbnail, and image. The same embed renderer works in channels, threads, and DMs.

Orbit APP

Weekend build night

Bring an idea. We’ll build it together.

When

Saturday, 8 PM

Where

#dev-talk

Community events · Today
JavaScript 
const embed = new EmbedBuilder()
  .setColor(Colors.Blurple)
  .setAuthor({ name: 'Orbit' })
  .setTitle('Weekend build night')
  .setURL('https://ipmingsum2.github.io/external/chat.html')
  .setDescription('Bring an idea. We’ll build it **together**.')
  .addFields(
    { name: 'When', value: 'Saturday, 8 PM', inline: true },
    { name: 'Where', value: '#dev-talk', inline: true }
  )
  .setFooter({ text: 'Community events' })
  .setTimestamp();
await channel.send({ content: 'You’re invited!', embeds: [embed] });
// Optional: .setImage('https://...') or .setThumbnail('https://...')

Use HTTPS for links and images. Limits: 10 embeds per message; 25 fields per embed; title 256 characters; description 4096; field name 256; field value 1024; footer 2048; combined embed text and URLs 6000. AutoMod checks embed content too. Raw HTML is not supported.

04

Direct messages

Bots can open a DM with a member and send text or embeds. A bot only sees DMs it participates in; it cannot inspect conversations between other people.

JavaScript 
const user = await client.users.fetch('MEMBER_UUID');
await user.send('Hello! Here is the update you requested.');

// Or respond privately to someone who asks:
client.on(Events.MessageCreate, async message => {
  if (!message.author.bot && message.content === '!helpme') {
    await message.author.send({ embeds: [
      new EmbedBuilder().setTitle('Help').setDescription('How can I help?')
    ] });
  }
});

DM creation is limited to 10 requests per minute per bot. Reopening the same conversation returns the same channel. Sending still follows message rate limits and AutoMod.

05

Moderation

Messaging works by default. Root can grant optional permissions in Apps & Bots → Permissions. Bots never receive human staff roles and cannot moderate staff or root.

Permission Allows
moderate Warn, mute, ban, unban, remove mute. The bot owner must still be Moderator or higher.
manage_messages Delete another member’s message in a channel the bot can view. AutoMod system alerts are protected.
automod Create, edit, and delete AutoMod rules. The owner must still be Administrator or higher.
JavaScript 
await client.moderation.warn(userId, 'Please follow the rules.', 'Message evidence');
await client.moderation.timeout(userId, 600, 'Repeated spam'); // seconds
await client.moderation.untimeout(userId, 'Appeal accepted');
await client.moderation.ban(userId, 'Spam', { seconds: 86400 });
await client.moderation.unban(userId, 'Appeal accepted');
// Omit seconds for a permanent ban. All actions require a reason.

Moderation actions are recorded in Account Standing. A revoked token or permission takes effect on subsequent requests. Bots under a warning, ban, or timeout cannot bypass their restriction.

06

Words, wildcards & AutoMod

Separate plain phrases with commas or new lines. Matching is case-insensitive. * matches additional characters within a word. Regex patterns are separate and stay one per line, so commas inside regex are preserved.

Keyword Matches Does not match
cat cat, cat! cats, bobcat
cat* cat, cats, caterpillar bobcat
*cat cat, bobcat cats
*cat* cats, bobcats dog

Detect words in your Node bot

JavaScript 
import { matchesWords } from './chatbox.js';
client.on(Events.MessageCreate, async message => {
  if (message.author.bot) return;
  if (matchesWords(message.content, ['spam*, unwanted phrase'], {
    allowedWords: ['spamton'], patterns: [/repeat\d+/i]
  })) {
    // Requires root-granted moderate permission.
    await client.moderation.warn(message.author.id, 'Please rephrase.', message.content);
  }
});

Bot handlers see messages after they are posted. Use server AutoMod to block content before it appears.

Configure server AutoMod

JavaScript 
await client.automod.save({
  id: 'my-bot-spam-rule', name: 'Spam phrases', enabled: true,
  words: ['spam*, unwanted phrase'], allowed_words: ['spamton'],
  patterns: ['repeat[0-9]+'], // PostgreSQL regex, not JavaScript RegExp
  block_message: 'Please keep the conversation on topic.',
  actions: ['warning', 'timeout'], timeout_seconds: 600,
  log_channel_id: 'PRIVATE_LOG_CHANNEL_ID'
});
await client.automod.delete('my-bot-spam-rule');

Rules always block matches. Optional actions are warning, timeout, and ban. Use ban_seconds for a temporary ban, or null for permanent. Omit the log channel to keep events staff-only. Plain keywords follow Discord’s wildcard approach; the regex engine here is PostgreSQL.

07

API reference

SDK Purpose
client.login(token?) Authenticate and start new-message polling
client.channels.fetch(id?) Fetch one channel or all visible channels
channel.send(string | {content, embeds}) Send a message
channel.messages.fetch({after, afterId}) Read up to 100 messages after a cursor
message.reply / edit / delete Reply, update your own message, or delete
client.users.fetch(id) Fetch a member profile
user.send(payload) / user.createDM() Send a DM or return its channel
client.cursor Current {after, afterId} polling cursor
client.destroy() Stop polling

HTTP endpoints

Base: https://lflkpziiwnoamvtrbcil.supabase.co/functions/v1/chat-api. Authenticate with Authorization: Bot YOUR_TOKEN.

Method Path
GET /v1/me
GET /v1/channels
GET /v1/events?after=ISO&after_id=ID
GET, POST /v1/channels/{id}/messages
PATCH, DELETE /v1/messages/{id}
GET /v1/users/{id}
POST /v1/dms
POST /v1/moderation
POST /v1/automod
DELETE /v1/automod/{id}

Message JSON uses text, embeds, and optional reply_to. The SDK maps content to text. DM JSON uses user_id. Moderation uses user_id, action, reason, optional expires_at (ISO date), and evidence.

08

Errors & compatibility

The API allows 60 requests/minute per bot and 30 message mutations/minute. Moderation is limited to 10 actions/minute. Slowmode applies unless the bot has Manage channel permission. Polling consumes API requests.

JavaScript 
try {
  await channel.send('Hello');
} catch (error) {
  if (error.status === 429) {
    console.log('Wait', error.retryAfter || 60, 'seconds before retrying.');
  } else if (error.blocked) {
    console.log('AutoMod:', error.message);
  } else {
    console.error(error.message);
  }
}

401: invalid/revoked token. 403: permission or validation failure. 422: AutoMod blocked the message. 429: rate limit or slowmode. Sends are not retried automatically, preventing accidental duplicates.

Store client.cursor outside the process for restart recovery, then pass it to new Client({cursor}). Message handlers should be idempotent. A failed handler is reported through the error event and the cursor advances; queue durable work yourself if retries are required.

Compatibility: chatbox.js is a small SDK for this CHATBOX server, with familiar Discord-style methods. It is not discord.js and cannot connect to Discord. It does not claim complete Discord feature parity. The older chatbox-bot.mjs helper remains supported.
